correctness.rationale: For each unordered pulse pair, direct interval intersection in the Wigner integral gives a sine-envelope channel supported on the midpoint interval. All such supports are disjoint by the quantified hypothesis, allowing separate spatial absolute values. The spatial integral is exactly J_l(xi)[S+2sum |aj ak| |cos phase|]/(pi*l*S*|xi|). Periodic |sin| and |cos| have mean 2/pi and bounded-primitive O(1) errors after 1/xi weighting. The signed Wigner integral over the symmetric cutoff is between 0 and 1 by the momentum marginal and Plancherel; negativity is half L1 minus signed mass. Thus the full infinite-R coefficient and O(1) remainder follow, not just a heuristic average. Cauchy--Schwarz yields the sharp equal-amplitude condition. Fresh independent interval-quadrature agrees with the exact spatial formula at four frequencies.

The explicit pair-interference contribution quantifies an observable effect of coherent superposition, sharply determines the fixed-N amplitude extremizers and an unbounded sequence of coefficients; the nontrivial midpoint separation is necessary to avoid overlapping signed channels. It is not mere restatement of the existence of Wigner interference or a numerical finite-cutoff table.
